simple.meaning: אַרְכִּי (ʼArkîy) is a Hebrew object word meaning “an Arkite or native of Erek.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Joshua 16:2. The surrounding context includes kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַרְכִּי (H757) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

firstOccurrence.englishText: It went out from Bethel to Luz, and passed along to the border of the Archites to Ataroth;

majorEvents.evidenceText: It went out from Bethel to Luz, and passed along to the border of the Archites to Ataroth;

timeline.evidenceText: It went out from Bethel to Luz, and passed along to the border of the Archites to Ataroth;
When David had come to the top, where God was worshiped, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his tunic torn, and earth on his head.
When Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, had come to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
Then Absalom said, “Now call Hushai the Archite also, and let’s hear likewise what he says.”

Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel.” For Yahweh had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that Yahweh might bring evil on Absalom.
Ahithophel was the king’s counselor. Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.

definitions.full: H757. Arki אַרְכִּי adjective, of a people (derivation unknown) applied to חוּשַׁי 2Sam 15:32 ; 16:16 ; 17:5 , 14 ; 1Chr 27:33 ; with article = collective noun הָא ׳גְּבוּל Josh 16:2 (not far from Bethel).
